Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 43, English)
Guru Tattva and the Pitru "Post": Bhaiya's Own Journey , and Why the Ancestor Seat Can Never Be Vacated

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn Mool T atva satsang on guru tattva, built ar ound Bhaiya's own extended personal origin story — adopting Hanuman Ji Maharaj as guru with no human intermediary , years of unexplained pitru harassment while building mantra dimension, a dir ect confr ontation with his own family's ancestors, and the r esulting teaching that pitru dosh is a permanent structural "post" in a person's birth chart that can never be eliminated — only pr otected against.
1. Session Opening and Today's Topic

1. Bhaiya welcomes newcomers to the "Mool Tatva" (foundational teaching) session series, noting that Third Eye batch aura-checking is nearly complete, with r emaining stragglers to be checked separately . He states today's session will focus specifically on guru tattva (the guru principle/element), approached from a somewhat dif ferent angle than previous discussions of the topic.
2. Bhaiya's Own Starting Point: A Guru With No Human Intermediary

1. Bhaiya r ecounts that he personally never took a living human guru — instead adopting Hanuman Ji Maharaj dir ectly as his guru, and choosing to chant "Jai Siyaram" as his mantra. 2. He explains that this specific mantra had a distinct disadvantage at the time: it had no "vin ि◌य ोग" (a mantra's formal ritual activation/awakening, historically performed and codified by a r ecognized saint) — meaning no established saint had ever fully "awakened" it thr ough their own body , and it carried no written scriptural explanation (vyakhyan) or codified use. Bhaiya states he initially received this as a real disadvantage.
3. The First 1.5 Years: Undisturbed Practice, Pr ecisely Because the Mantra Was Unr ecognized

1. After completing his graduation, Bhaiya committed to r oughly 10 hours of daily practice (br oken into multiple 2-hour sitting blocks), and for the first year and a half, he encounter ed no interfer ence or problems whatsoever . 2. This teaching's explanation for that undisturbed period: his family's ancestors (pitru) simply did not r ecognize "Jai Siyaram" as an established, thr eatening mantra — since it carried no known vin ि◌योग, they had no frame of reference for what he was actually doing, and so did not interfere at all during this stage.
4. Around 2.5 Cr or e Japa: The First Signs, and External Doubt

1. Once Bhaiya's japa count cr ossed r oughly two and a half cr or e (25 million) r epetitions, subtle physical signs began appearing — a faint inner luminosity/glow within the body — and pitru influence began, in a small way , for the first time. 2. Around this period, after moving to Gurgaon, Bhaiya sought outside verification fr om established saints and was told repeatedly that "Jai Siyaram" carried no r eal shakti, and that he should switch to a mor e conventional, established
mantra like "Om Hanumate Namah" instead. Bhaiya states he seriously considered abandoning his practice at points during this stretch, but ultimately did not switch mantras.
5. Three Years In: Active Pitru Interfer ence Begins

1. After roughly thr ee years of sustained practice, pitru began actively tr oubling Bhaiya — appearing in dr eams to physically weaken him and for cibly wake him, along with the onset of minor physical binding sensations (leg pain, lack of motivation, family friction) — described as pitru gradually testing whether his gr owing practice posed a genuine threat to their influence.
6. Five Cr or e Japa: The Body Becomes Unr eachable, So Attacks Move Outward

1. By the time Bhaiya's japa cr ossed r oughly five cr or e (50 million) r epetitions, his body had become fully saturated/surr ounded by mantra energy , making it impossible for any pitru to physically enter it any longer . 2. Once direct bodily entry was no longer possible, this teaching states pitru shifted to external, cir cumstantial sabotage instead — deliberately blocking desir ed outcomes in daily life (illustrated via a popular comedy bit about a r ed shirt never being available the one day you need it) — r eframed her e not as random bad luck, but as ancestors specifically ensuring nothing in the practitioner's life goes smoothly , hoping to psychologically br eak their resolve.
7. Moments of Doubt, and the Guru's Refusal to Let Him Quit

1. Bhaiya candidly describes r epeated urges to abandon the practice during this period, and moments of comparing himself unfavorably to intensely devoted r enunciants (illustratively , ascetics standing in tapasya for years to r eceive even a brief divine glimpse), feeling demoralized by comparison. 2. He states that although his guru could have let him give up, his guru never allowed this — appearing to him nightly to teach him dir ectly , redirecting him whenever he seriously consider ed quitting, and never removing his ability to chant the name even during his weakest moments of doubt.
8. Manifestation, Siddhi, and the Revelation of the Ancestors

1. Continued practice eventually led to Prabhu's dir ect manifestation (pratyaksh darshan) and blessing; r oughly six to eight months after this manifestation, siddhi was granted, after which drishti activated fully . 2. Once drishti opened, the very first thing Bhaiya r eports seeing clearly was that his own family's ancestors (pitru) had been the ones r esponsible for the years of obstruction he had personally experienced.
9. Confr onting the Family's Decade-Long Pitru Bhog Practice

1. Bhaiya r ecounts his family's practice of offering daily pitru bhog (ancestor food offerings) continuously for over ten years — a practice his father never stopped and that Bhaiya, lacking pr oof at the time, never previously challenged. 2. Once people Bhaiya had personally advised to chant "Jai Siyaram" began experiencing r esolved crises and opened drishti of their own, his father began taking Bhaiya's path mor e seriously and eventually began asking him dir ectly about it.
10. Dir ect Confr ontation With the Ancestors, and the Water Kavach

1. Bhaiya r ecounts dir ectly and r espectfully asking his family's ancestors, thr ough drishti, to leave the household — initially received calmly , but the ancestors then consulted several other entities and grew aggressive, escalating to a dramatic show of collective force ("doli aa gayi"). 2. In response, Bhaiya sought his guru's help and was taught a specific vidya to construct a pr otective "water kavach" (jal kavach), which he used to expel all the ancestors fr om the household — they remained outside, verbally hostile but unable
to act against him personally , and the household enjoyed four days of genuine peace afterward.
1 1. The Fifth-Day Retaliation, the Father's Accident, and the Guru's Doot

1. On the fifth day , as Bhaiya's father was driving, this teaching describes the ancestors r etaliating via a pr e-negotiated territorial arrangement with a local entity (having offer ed it ten days' worth of bhog in exchange for cooperation) — causing the father to briefly lose consciousness, r esulting in a minor collision. 2. At that exact critical moment, Bhaiya's guru's doot (messenger , described as a sturdy , bear -like being) intervened directly , reviving the father from unconsciousness befor e serious harm occurr ed — appearing visibly exhausted and "wounded" afterward fr om the effort of this r escue. 3. That evening, Bhaiya's guru showed him the full scene in vivid clarity thr ough drishti: the two contesting shaktis, the ancestors' prior territorial bhog-negotiation, and the doot's timely r escue — this direct evidence finally convinced Bhaiya's father that the family's troubles were genuinely pitru-related, not superstition, with Bhaiya noting that a familiar guru's or parent's specific manner of discipline is recognizable precisely because of years of close relational familiarity ("a mother's hit feels like a mother's hit; a father's hit feels like a father's hit").
12. The Father's Permission, and the Guru's Formal Ritual Resolution

1. Bhaiya's father subsequently gave him explicit permission to act fr eely against the family's ancestors, a diagnosis independently corr oborated by Bhaiya's younger brother , who also had his own drishti. 2. That same night, Bhaiya's guru had him construct a four -mouthed (chaturmukha) hawan kund, divided into eight sections, forming a special ritual lok and teaching him specific new vidyas — the next day , five generations of family ancestors were sent for 28 days of "tadna" (a purification/disciplinary process). 3. Nearly all of these ancestors, upon r eturning fr om this pr ocess, had been permanently transferr ed to Kalyan Lok (a purification r ealm) — only one or two initially resisted and retained their defiance until as late as day 45, before eventually pledging cooperation and being sent onward to "Pretraj Sarkar" (a further ancestral administrative authority).
13. The Guru's Reframe: Pitru Were Never Enemies — They Were Surveillance

1. Bhaiya's guru continues to r emind him that one's own ancestors can attack at any time, and that daily pitru prayer (prarthana) should ther efor e never be neglected, r egardless of past r esolution. 2. The guru's cor e reframing of the entir e ordeal: the family's ancestors wer e never truly enemies — they functioned as a kind of surveillance/testing mechanism, attacking specifically at moments of weakness or error , genuinely believing they were holding Bhaiya back, while in fact their pressure was what for ced him to become mor e resilient and steadily increase his subtle-body "dimension."
14. The Mechanical Explanation: Why the Interfer ence Actually Helped

1. This teaching explains that awakening guru tattva thr ough any given mantra r equires roughly five cr or e (50 million) units of accumulated subtle-body "dimension," which in turn r equires roughly 5,000 cumulative hours of seated practice at one consistent location — described her e as "asana siddhi is dir ectly pr oportional to dimension." 2. A key supporting observation: practitioners whose drishti opens quickly (within a month, say) typically stop practicing further once their immediate personal crisis r esolves, never accumulating the full 5,000 hours — whereas pitru harassment, by deliberately sabotaging every other life avenue for a serious long-term practitioner , inadvertently keeps that practitioner sitting in continued practice (since nothing else seems likely to succeed anyway) until the full threshold is eventually crossed regardless of the pitru's intent.** 3. This teaching clarifies that the pitru interfer ence during this period was never really about draining "energy" as commonly assumed — the actual operative unit was always the 5,000-hour dimension thr eshold, not energy depletion per se.
15. The Threshold Cr ossing: Rising Permanently Above the Ancestors' Reach

1. This teaching states that the instant a practitioner crosses their required dimension/hour threshold, an automatic shift occurs — the guru elevates the practitioner directly above the r each of their own ancestors, who r etain their nominal structural position but can no longer touch the practitioner personally , having fallen "lakhs" of dimension-levels behind.
16. Pitru Dosh as an Unr emovable Structural "Post" in the Birth Chart

1. This teaching's central structural claim: pitru dosh is not about any one specific tr oublesome ancestor — it is an inherent, un-eliminable "post" or designated seat within a person's own birth chart (janma kundli), dir ectly comparable to other permanent cosmic "posts" like Indra's or Ganesh's. 2. Because this is a structural featur e of the kundli itself, it cannot be destr oyed or permanently vacated — sending one specific troublesome ancestor onward via mukti rituals or pind-daan simply cr eates a vacancy in that same designated seat, which will inevitably be filled by another entity (not necessarily even a biological r elative) who will continue performing the exact same assigned "duty ." 3. An illustrative analogy offer ed: this is comparable to asking God to permanently r emove a bodily organ (like a hand) from existence for all futur e children — you cannot simply delete a fundamental structural featur e this way .
17. Why Aghori and Pind-Daan Traditions Don't Permanently Solve This Either

1. This teaching states that full r enunciation traditions (like becoming an aghori) or extensive pind-daan rituals do not permanently fr ee a person fr om the pitru cycle — of fered evidence: only roughly two out of ten aghoris (by Bhaiya's own estimate) actually achieve genuine siddhi, specifically those whose own ancestors happen to already be favorably disposed toward supporting them. If renunciation alone were suf ficient, this teaching ar gues, all aghoris would achieve siddhi uniformly , which is demonstrably not observed.
18. A Live Illustration: A Protective Devta Blocking Someone's Third Eye

1. During this same session's aura-checking pr ocess, Bhaiya describes discovering that a r eal Himalayan folk deity ("Golu Devta") was actively , protectively blocking a specific person's third-eye opening — traced to a household diya specifically dedicated to that devta, drawing its protective presence, which was deliberately preventing drishti from opening for its own protective reasons. 2. This is offer ed as a parallel example of the same "unr emovable structural post" principle applying even at the devta level — some structur es and postings simply cannot and should not be for cibly r emoved, even when they cr eate an obstacle for the practitioner .
19. Practical Guidance for Someone Under Active Pitru Dosh

1. This teaching's practical r ecommendation: rather than attempting to eliminate pitru dosh entir ely (which this teaching states is structurally impossible), a person should identify exactly which specific activities their particular ancestral post-holder currently "permits" them to do, and deliberately multiply and intensify effort specifically within those permitted channels — precisely mirroring Bhaiya's own personal path — until they personally cross their own threshold and rise directly above the post's structural reach. 2. A specific diagnostic clarification is offer ed: genuine, active pitru dosh manifests as concr ete physical symptoms (body pain, shoulder pain, leg pain) — if these specific physical symptoms ar e absent, a person is not curr ently under active pitru dosh, r egardless of how many ancestors may be visible hovering ar ound them; conversely , if these specific symptoms ar e present, whichever entity curr ently occupies the household's "pitru seat" is r esponsible, r egardless of whether that ancestor is personally favorably or unfavorably disposed toward the individual affected.

3. An illustrative "wheat allergy" analogy is offer ed: someone allergic to wheat doesn't demand the world's entir e wheat supply be destr oyed, since it nourishes and benefits others — similarly , someone bother ed by pitru dosh shouldn't seek to eliminate the entir e ancestor concept, but should simply stop actively "feeding"/worshipping that specific occupied seat and instead pray specifically for protection of their own seat. 4. The specific, concr ete practical r equest recommended during hawan or personal worship: ask for a "pitru kavach" (ancestor shield) — protection ensuring that nothing occupies one's own personal seat — rather than attempting to remove pitru dosh altogether , which this teaching maintains is not structurally possible.
20. A Household Example: Ten Ancestors, Mixed Disposition, Same Physical Symptoms

1. This teaching addr esses a live example of one household having ten ancestors, five favorably disposed and five not: it clarifies that even if every single one wer e favorably disposed, whichever one occupies the household's designated "pitru seat" will still cause the same physical symptoms in a descendant's body , purely as a function of holding that seat/office — independent of that specific ancestor's personal disposition toward the individual affected. 2. This is extended into a br oader debt (rin) analogy: pitru dosh functions like an unpayable debt that can never be fully and permanently discharged — no amount of pind-daan or ritual work permanently "clears the account," since sending one ancestor onward via mukti simply cr eates a vacancy that another will inevitably fill.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Bhaiya's own mantra ("Jai Siyaram") went undisturbed for 1.5 years specifically because it had no formal "vin ि◌य ोग" (ritual activation) that his family's ancestors r ecognized as a r eal thr eat — active pitru interference only began once his practice accumulated enough dimension (starting around 2.5 crore japa) to become noticeable. Once a practitioner's body becomes fully saturated with mantra energy (ar ound 5 cr or e japa in Bhaiya's own case), pitru can no longer enter the body dir ectly — so they shift to external, cir cumstantial sabotage instead , deliberately blocking desired outcomes to test and wear down resolve. Awakening guru tattva thr ough a mantra r equires roughly 5 cr or e units of accumulated subtle-body "dimension," corr esponding to r oughly 5,000 cumulative hours of seated practice — practitioners whose drishti opens quickly typically stop practicing before reaching this threshold, while sustained pitru interference (by sabotaging every other life avenue) can inadvertently keep a serious practitioner sitting until the threshold is crossed regardless. Pitru were never truly enemies in this teaching's r eframing — they function as a surveillance/testing mechanism , attacking specifically at moments of weakness while genuinely believing they're holding the practitioner back, when their pressure is what actually builds resilience and dimension. Pitru dosh is not about any one specific tr oublesome ancestor — it is a permanent, un-eliminable structural "post" within a person's own birth chart , directly comparable to other permanent cosmic posts (like Indra's or Ganesh's); removing one specific ancestor from this seat via mukti or pind-daan only creates a vacancy that another entity will inevitably fill. Full renunciation (aghori traditions) or extensive pind-daan does not permanently fr ee someone fr om this cycle either — only ancestors already favorably disposed toward supporting a renunciant produce genuine siddhi, which is why only a minority of aghoris (roughly two out of ten, by this teaching's estimate) actually attain it. Genuine, active pitru dosh always manifests as concr ete physical symptoms (body , shoulder , or leg pain) — absence of these symptoms means a person is not currently under active pitru dosh, regardless of how many ancestors are visible; presence of these symptoms means whichever entity occupies the "pitru seat" is responsible, regardless of that entity's personal disposition. The practical, structurally possible r equest is a "pitru kavach" (pr otective shield over one's own seat) — not elimination of pitru dosh itself , which this teaching states cannot be structurally removed, much like a protective devta's post (illustrated by a real "Golu Devta" example) cannot simply be removed even when it creates an obstacle.

The recommended practical strategy under active pitru dosh: identify exactly which specific activities one's ancestral post curr ently "permits," and deliberately intensify effort within exactly those permitted channels until personally rising above the post's structural r each — exactly mirroring Bhaiya's own documented personal journey .
